source_document.body:
The North Mara gold mine in Tanzania. Credit: Barrick Mining
Posted By: Colin McClelland November 27, 2026
Barrick Mining (TSX: ABX; NYSE: B) has given mine managers more responsibility in setting and meeting production targets after years of missed forecasts eroded investor confidence in the world’s third-largest gold miner by 2025 output, Barrick International CEO Sebastiaan Bock said.
Barrick had made a habit of issuing three-year production forecasts and resetting them a year later, hurting credibility, group CEO Mark Hill told Mining Forum Americas in Colorado Springs, Colo., in September. As Barrick prepares to float its North American gold business as American Barrick Gold (proposed NYSE: ABGC), Bock said the international operations he now oversees have collectively met or exceeded annual production guidance for seven straight years.
“A year ago, we worked with mine leaders to rebuild our guidance from the ground up, and we gave them more responsibility and accountability for meeting their new targets,” Bock said in emailed replies this month. “In 2027, investors should judge us by whether we continue to improve safety, meet our guidance, control costs, and deliver our growth projects on time and on budget.”
The landmark initial public offering , expected by early next year, will give investors direct exposure to Barrick’s interests in Nevada Gold Mines, the Fourmile gold project in Nevada and Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic. The Toronto-based parent intends to retain majority ownership of the new company while developing its international gold and copper assets, including the Lumwana expansion in Zambia and the delayed Reko Diq project in Pakistan.
Barrick shares more than doubled last year but have shed about 26% since closing February at $69.21. They gained 3.7% to $51.70 apiece in Toronto by mid-Friday, valuing the company at about $84 billion. The stock is down 11% from a year ago.
Q&A
The Northern Miner managed to catch up by email with a busy Bock, who was appointed in August, for a brief Q&A on his priorities for 2027. While he wasn’t permitted to discuss the IPO, he addressed everything from rising copper costs and mine safety to the challenges of delivering multibillion-dollar projects.
The Northern Miner: Mark Hill has made rebuilding Barrick’s credibility a priority. Within your international business, what has changed in mine planning, management accountability and incentives? Which measurable results should investors judge you on in 2027?
Sebastiaan Bock: A year ago, we worked with mine leaders to rebuild our guidance from the ground up, and we gave them more responsibility and accountability for meeting their new targets. That approach is consistent with Barrick’s historical culture of decentralization that drove our past successes, and it is working.
We have also advanced our growth projects, Lumwana most importantly, on time and on budget. And we did it all while prioritizing and improving safety, because we know from experience that a safe mine is a productive mine.
Barrick International — our portfolio combining Barrick’s Africa & Middle East and South America & Asia Pacific regions — remains on track to meet full-year guidance and has met or exceeded production guidance for seven consecutive years. In 2027, investors should judge us by whether we continue to improve safety, meet our guidance, control costs, and deliver our growth projects on time and on budget.
Barrick International CEO Sebastiaan Bock. Credit: Barrick Mining
Copper costs
TNM: Barrick’s third-quarter copper all-in sustaining costs reached $4.52 per lb., against annual guidance of $3.45–$3.75. How much of the pressure reflects fuel and currencies, and how much reflects operating performance? What can you improve in 2027?
SB: The $4.52 per pound is a quarterly figure, and year to date we are at $4.05. As we said at our third-quarter results , we expect full-year copper costs at or very slightly above the top of the range. The principal drivers were higher diesel prices, local currency appreciation, higher royalties linked to stronger copper prices, and additional waste stripping.
Operating factors also contributed, including Lumwana bringing a planned mill reline forward to late September, which deferred higher-grade ore to October and lowered [Barrick’s total copper] production from 56,000 to 50,000 tonnes in the third quarter. Full-year production guidance of 190,000 to 220,000 tonnes is unchanged.
Safety
TNM: What are the biggest remaining challenges in safety across your operations, and what specific changes have you introduced? What measures will show whether those changes are working in 2027?
SB: Safety is Barrick’s number one priority globally. Our recordable injury frequency is improving, and the principal remaining challenge is severity. Leaders now verify critical controls directly in the field. They completed more than 24,000 verifications in the third quarter, of which 79% of the at-risk conditions identified were resolved on the spot.
We have invested more than US$90 million in safety technology, including automation, vehicle monitoring systems, safety reporting software, and AI-based analytics. In 2027, progress will be measured by TRIFR [total recordable injury frequency rate] and lost-time injury frequency each quarter, and by the quality of our verifications.
Lumwana
TNM: The Lumwana expansion in Zambia remains scheduled for first copper at the end of the first quarter of 2028. Which construction milestones must you meet in 2027, and what poses the greatest risk to the budget or timetable?
SB: Lumwana is an exciting growth project for us, and it is progressing well. The project remains on budget and on schedule for first copper at the end of the first quarter of 2028. All major long-lead equipment has been procured. The mill building, which sits on the project’s critical path, remains scheduled for completion this quarter.
In 2027, the focus moves to mechanical installation, the start of commissioning, and the ramp-up of mining. As with any project of this scale, our priority is disciplined execution. We have an experienced team, which knows to plan early for power, equipment, and logistics. We expect the expansion to double Lumwana’s copper production.
The security environment, financing plan and capital estimate will determine Reko Diq’s pace, Bock said. Credit: Barrick Mining.
Reko Diq
TNM: With development slowed and the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Pakistan under review, what conditions must be met before work can accelerate? When do you expect to provide a revised assessment of costs, financing and the production timetable?
SB: In April we slowed development and extended our review in light of the security situation in the region, which we are assessing alongside capital requirements, financing, scope, and timeline.
We expect to provide an update on the review by mid-2027. Any acceleration will depend first on the security environment and then on a financing plan and capital estimate in which we have full confidence. We continue to regard Reko Diq as one of the world’s largest undeveloped copper-gold projects.
Operating reliability
TNM: North Mara in Tanzania, Veladero in Argentina and Porgera in Papua New Guinea have faced different operating disruptions this year. Which problems have been resolved, and what changes will make their production plans more dependable in 2027?
SB: Every operation faces its own distinct challenges. For example, Veladero and Porgera were affected by weather events. Severe winter storms at Veladero temporarily suspended operations on several occasions during the third quarter, and water shortages associated with El Niño reduced plant operating rates at Porgera.
At North Mara, local grid instability affected underground performance and plant run-time. We are addressing it through multiple projects, including a STATCOM [voltage stabilizer] installation expected to be completed by mid-2027. Production at North Mara rose 6% from the second quarter to the third, and we expect to increase mining of higher-grade open pit material in the fourth quarter.
While weather-related disruptions affected Veladero and Porgera, stronger performances from Loulo-Gounkoto, Kibali, Bulyanhulu, and North Mara have kept Barrick International on track to achieve its full-year production guidance.

source_document.body:
A used 2026 Cyberbeast listed at $150,790 (Screenshot: CarGurus)
Used Cybertruck prices are up 10 to 15% in the month since Tesla announced it would end production of its electric pickup, according to listing data from CarGurus and Visor.
Some dealers are pushing it much further. One in New Jersey now wants $150,790 for a used Cyberbeast, about $36,000 more than Tesla charges for a brand-new one.
The numbers
CarGurus’ price index puts the average used Cybertruck at $89,715, up 9.84% over the last 30 days and 13.5% over 90 days. Over the same 30 days, the broader used car market went down 1.37%.
Visor, which tracks dealer listings hourly and compares the same trucks month to month, shows a bigger move: +15% like-for-like versus last month, with an average asking price of $101,784 across 171 used trucks. Listings that sold in the last 30 days took 17 days on average.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The curve on CarGurus’ chart is flat at around $80,000 from July to late October. Then it bends up in November.
That lines up exactly with Tesla’s moves. On November 6, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas, and Tesla raised prices by up to 10% the same day . A week later, Tesla stopped selling every Cybertruck except the Cyberbeast at $109,990. And this week, it bumped the Cyberbeast again to $114,990, which is what Tesla’s configurator shows today.
In early August, the cheapest Cybertruck you could order was $69,990. Now it’s $114,990.
The craziest listing
Sorting CarGurus’ nationwide used Cybertruck inventory by price, the top listing is a 2026 Cyberbeast with 4,493 miles at J&S AutoHaus in Ewing, New Jersey. The asking price is $150,790 with fees.
A used 2026 Cyberbeast listed at $150,790 (Screenshot: CarGurus)
CarGurus flags it as “Overpriced” and says it’s $35,773 above market. But the price history is the best part.
The dealer listed it at $134,995 on November 20. It went to $139,995 on November 25, the day after Tesla’s latest $5,000 Cyberbeast hike, and then to $149,995 the next day. That’s $15,000 in six days on a truck nobody has saved yet, according to CarGurus.
The same dealer also has a 2026 Cyberbeast with 851 miles at $145,790. Elsewhere, a 2024 Cyberbeast with 302 miles in Calumet City, Illinois, is listed at $148,816. And a 2024 dual-motor AWD with 1,500 miles in Lincoln, Nebraska, is at $145,306. That’s more than the $99,990 Tesla charged for a fully loaded Foundation Series AWD back in 2024.
Canadian dealers are playing the same game. The most expensive listing on AutoTrader.ca right now is a 2024 Cyberbeast with 1 km in Mississauga at C$199,999. The other 13 priced listings in the country sit between C$105,000 and C$141,995.
The other end of the market
Sort the same CarGurus inventory from the bottom, though, and the picture changes.
A 2025 AWD with 22,495 miles is listed at $68,619 in San Bernardino, California. A 2024 Cyberbeast with 65,482 miles is at $70,118. There are several 2024 AWD trucks with 20,000 to 40,000 miles in the $77,000 to $80,000 range, and CarGurus rates many of them as good or great deals.
So the floor didn’t move all that much. What moved is the top and the middle.
There’s another detail in the CarGurus data. The 2024 model year is up 11.68% in 30 days, to $91,220. The 2025 model year is flat at $80,979, with 0% change over the same period.
The 2024 trucks include the Foundation Series, which came with Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving” package bought outright. Tesla now only sells FSD as a subscription, so those trucks have something new ones don’t. The 2025s, mostly the cheaper AWD trims, aren’t getting the same bump.
Electrek’s Take
It’s good news for current owners who want out. Many of them watched their trucks lose about half their value between 2024 and 2025. This is the best window they’ve had in a long time.

Tesla made the cheaper versions impossible to order, so used trucks are now the only way to get anything other than a $115,000 Cyberbeast. That pushes the middle of the market up. And part of it is just dealers testing what people will pay. These are asking prices.

Aerial view of the Simandou project area. (Image courtesy of Rio Tinto).
By: Staff Writer November 27, 2026
Rio Tinto (NYSE, LSE, ASX: RIO) has shipped the first Europe-bound iron ore cargo from Guinea’s giant Simandou project , expanding its market beyond China.
The Tower Point left Morebaya anchorage on Nov. 23 carrying about 79,100 tonnes of Simandou iron ore fines sold by SimFer, commodities data and analytics firm Kpler said Friday . SimFer is the Rio Tinto-led venture that operates Simandou’s two southern mining blocks.
The vessel is expected in Dunkirk, France, on Dec. 4. Luxembourg-based ArcelorMittal (NYSE: MT) operates a steelworks there. A second Europe-bound cargo is being loaded aboard the True Caspian for delivery to Gijón, Spain, where ArcelorMittal also has steelmaking operations, according to Kpler.
Simandou began exporting ore in December 2025, with its initial cargoes going to China. The high-grade deposit offers steelmakers an alternative source of ore as they seek to reduce emissions.
Source: Kpler Insight.
ArcelorMittal, the world’s second-largest steelmaker after China Baowu Steel Group, produces nearly 50 million tonnes of iron ore annually from its own mines, covering more than 70% of its requirements.
Ramp-up
SimFer reached an annual production rate of about 10 million tonnes in the third quarter, Rio Tinto said. The venture targets a rate of 60 million tonnes a year in the second half of 2028; the wider Simandou development is designed to export up to 120 million tonnes annually.
Guinea’s monthly iron ore exports surpassed 5 million tonnes for the first time in October. Year-to-date shipments had exceeded 22 million tonnes, shipping association BIMCO reported in a Nov. 18 update.
Rio Tinto and a Chinalco-led consortium are developing Simandou’s southern blocks through SimFer, while Winning Consortium Simandou is developing the northern blocks. Guinea holds 15% of each mining venture. The partners share a rail and port infrastructure system.
Wealth fund
The growing trade comes as Guinea prepares to set aside mining revenue for long-term investment. The country’s National Assembly approved legislation establishing a sovereign wealth fund on Nov. 25. The text will go to President Mamadi Doumbouya for promulgation, the government said Thursday.
The fund’s initial capital target is $1 billion (C$1.4 billion), to be raised over no more than five years, according to the presidency. Planned funding includes 30% of taxes and other state revenue from Simandou and 5% of revenue from new extractive projects, the government said.
Under Guinea’s Simandou 2040 development programme, the fund would invest in infrastructure, energy, industry and local mineral processing, while building savings for future generations. A separate reserve would help cushion public finances against commodity price swings, according to official accounts.
The state-owned fund would have nine directors, including seven independent members. Its proposed safeguards include annual external audits and published financial statements. Withdrawals from savings for future generations would require approval from both the board and parliament and could not pay for routine government spending, the government said.

Posted By: Henry Lazenby November 27, 2026
Entrée Resources (TSX: ETG; US-OTC: ERLFF) and the Mongolian government have agreed to work towards a deal by the end of March 2027 on two mining licences that have held up underground development at Oyu Tolgoi’s Hugo North Extension copper-gold deposit, the company said Friday.
At issue is whether the state takes a stake of up to 34% in Entrée LLC, the subsidiary that holds the Shivee Tolgoi and Javkhlant mining licences, or accepts a royalty instead. Mongolia’s Parliament has the final say. The joint venture property lies about 570 km south of Ulaanbaatar.
Crews had completed about 230 equivalent metres of lateral development on Shivee Tolgoi by May 30, 2025, a week before Entrée announced the pause. Resolving the dispute so work can resume there would mark “a pivotal moment in Entrée’s 25-year history,” CEO Chris Adams wrote in a Sept. 28 shareholder letter.
Entrée holds a 20% carried interest in Hugo North Extension. Its partner, mine operator Oyu Tolgoi LLC, needs the licences in its name before crews can resume development there. Work has continued elsewhere at the mine. The operator expects Panel 1, which extends onto Shivee Tolgoi, to be the last section of the first underground level to enter production.
Entrée shares gained 7¢, or 3.3%, to $2.19 in Toronto at 12:53 p.m. Eastern time Friday, valuing the Vancouver-based company at about $486 million (US$341 million).
Royalty proposal
Mongolia already owns 34% of Oyu Tolgoi LLC. Rio Tinto (LSE, ASX, NYSE: RIO) owns the other 66% and expects the open pit and underground mine together to produce an average of 500,000 tonnes of copper a year from 2028 through 2036.
In March, Entrée offered to pay the state a royalty on the gross sales value of its share of concentrate. The company said it received no formal response and will prepare a revised offer.
Under the terms the two sides agreed to on Nov. 9 and 10, they can extend talks beyond March by mutual consent. Mongolia’s state news agency Montsame reported Thursday that the next round of talks is scheduled for January.
The licence transfer also requires tax payment certificates. Mongolia’s tax authority told Entrée LLC it couldn’t issue them because the documents supporting the licence valuations were incomplete, according to Entrée’s third-quarter report.
Underground drilling
Entrée also released assays Friday from seven underground holes its partner drilled at Hugo North Extension between 2023 and 2026. Hole UGD1025A cut 125.3 metres grading 1.28% copper, 0.27 gram gold and 3.18 grams silver per tonne from 362.7 metres downhole. Hole UGD918A, drilled along the mineralized trend, returned 67.6 metres grading 0.95% copper, 0.203 gram gold and 2.19 grams silver per tonne from 438.6 metres.
Crews drilled from existing workings on the operator’s own licence into the proposed second underground level, known as Lift 2, or the surrounding rock. The intervals are downhole lengths. For holes drilled across the mineralized trend, Entrée estimates true widths at 20% to 70% of the reported lengths.
Entrée aims to complete an updated technical report on its joint venture interest in the first quarter of 2027. It will incorporate a new resource model for Hugo North, including the extension, and a revised mine plan and production schedule for the first underground level.

MCACN 2026 Yenko Galore: From the 1966 Corvair Stinger to the 1981 Camaro Turbo Z
12 photos
Photo: The Supercar Registry/YouTube
Opened in 1949 in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, Yenko Chevrolet was no average dealership. In addition to selling common cars, Yenko also produced its very own vehicles. The Yenko Chevrolets are now among the most desirable performance cars from the golden era.
Yenko started out with a Durant dealership in 1929. It was opened by Frank Yenko, who in 1934 switched to selling Chevrolets. In 1957, Don Yenko, who was Frank's son, assumed ownership of the dealership. Nine years later, Yenko prepped a Corvair Corsa for SCCA racing and built 100 cars to obtain certification.
It was called the Yenko Stinger, and it was followed by many other Chevrolets through 1972. In 1981, one year before Don sold the business, Yenko produced its final batch of high-performance cars.
In all, Yenko modified five Chevrolet nameplates and rolled out vehicles for seven model years. All of them are quite rare, with production numbers ranging from a dozen to 200 units. Seeing two Yenkos at the same event is very rare, which is why the Yenko display at this year's MCACN was downright spectacular. It included one of each model built from 1966 to 1981.
Photo: The Supercar Registry/YouTube The Corvair-based Yenko Stinger is the oldest Yenko creation on display. Don completed 100 examples, which were all painted white and with blue stripes. However, the cars had different exterior mods, with some featuring fiberglass hoods and spoilers, while others came with upgraded engines. Yenko completed another 14 examples in 1967, while some sources suggest that a final car was built in 1969.
The Yenko Camaro, Don's most iconic creation, emerged in 1967. Also dubbed Yenko Super Cars, these Camaros were equipped with 427-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) V8 engines, which weren't available in the factory-built Camaro. Yenko used the L72, usually offered in the Corvette and the full-size cars.
The 1967 and 1968 Camaros were modified at Yenko's shop, but the 1969 version had its L72 installed by Chevrolet. That's because they were ordered through GM's COPO program . Yenko built 54 Camaros in 1967 and another 64 units in 1968. In 1969, Yenko ordered 198 COPO Camaros (Chevy eventually sold about 1,000 units).
The MCACN display included two 1967 Camaros, including the only known example fitted with side exhaust pipes. A 1968 Camaro and a 1969 COPO were also present, as well as a 1969 Z28 sold by the dealership (with no modifications).
Photo: The Supercar Registry/YouTube The Camaro wasn't the only Chevy that Yenko created through the COPO program. The dealership also ordered 99 Chevelles. These cars were also fitted with the 427 L72 engine. Chevrolet eventually sold a total of 323 examples. The one shown at MCACN is one of only six examples known to still exist.
1969 also saw the arrival of the Yenko Nova. Also ordered through the COPO program and fitted with the same L72 mill, the original Yenko Nova was by far the hottest compact put together in 1969. Only 38 cars were built, and one sold for a whopping $852,500 in early 2026.
Yenko rolled out a new Nova version in 1970, this time around fitted with the 350-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) LT1 V8. Unsurprisingly, Yenko used the COPO system to install the powerplant otherwise available in the Camaro Z28 and Corvette. This Nova is called the Deuce and was produced in 175 units. The MCACN display included two examples.
With muscle cars no longer popular in 1971, Yenko switched to the Chevrolet Vega subcompact. Also called the Stinger II, the Yenko Vega rolled out of the Chevrolet factory with four-cylinder engines fitted with heavy-duty forged aluminum pistons. These were designed to handle boost from the turbocharger kit offered by Yenko.
Photo: The Supercar Registry/YouTube The dealership sold 200 units per year in 1971 and 1972, with an additional unit put together as a giveaway car in 1973. That year, Yenko stopped building vehicles, opting to focus on aftermarket Stinger parts. Only 11 of the 400 Yenko Vegas are known to exist today. A 1972 example was displayed at MCACN.
In 1981, however, Yenko produced one final automobile. It was based on the 1981 Camaro Z28 and featured a body kit inspired by the IROC race cars. Power came from a 350-cubic-inch V8 engine topped by a turbocharger. The Turbo Z came with 250 horsepower on tap, which was quite impressive from the era. For reference, the factory Z28 was rated at 175 horsepower. Only 19 units were produced.
If you didn't make it to MCACN 2026, thus missing your shot at seeing every Yenko car under the same roof, the videos below include detailed walkarounds of the display. You'll also spot a 1981 Chevrolet Corvette that was sold by Yenko without aftermarket modifications. Tell me which your favorite Yenko is in the comments section below.
And in case you missed it, you should also check out the Chrysler 300 "letter series" display , which included every version of the iconic performance car built from 1955 to 1965.

Prevost H3-45 Electric (Image: Prevost)
Prevost, the Quebec coach builder owned by Volvo Group, has unveiled the H3-45 Electric, its first battery-electric motorcoach. It gets a 540 kWh Volvo battery, 450 kW (600 hp) from two electric motors, and both CCS1 and MCS charging as standard.
The H3-45 is Prevost’s flagship and one of the most common highway coaches in North America. Prevost is pitching the electric version as the same coach drivers and technicians already know, with a different powertrain.
Prevost first committed to an electric coach back in April 2022, when it announced a five-year electrification program backed by the Quebec government. That plan included a 100% electric coach and a retrofit kit to convert existing diesel coaches. The coach is now here. Prevost hasn’t said anything new about the retrofit kit.
The Prevost H3-45 Electric (Image: Prevost)
A Volvo powertrain in a Prevost body
Everything that moves the coach comes from Volvo. Prevost’s product page describes a single drive unit that combines two electric motors, an 8-speed automated manual transmission, and an oil retarder, rated at 450 kW (600 hp). Prevost’s tagline for it is “more power than diesel.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The Volvo dual-motor drive unit with integrated 8-speed transmission (Image: Prevost)
The gearbox is the interesting part. Volvo’s own BZR Electric coach chassis in Europe uses a 2-speed automated transmission, but a 45-foot North American coach spends most of its life at highway speed and on long grades, and more gears help keep the motors in their efficient range. Prevost claims 97% motor efficiency across the working range, and drivers get adjustable regenerative braking for descents.
540 kWh, but 459 kWh usable
The battery system is made of six Volvo Cube2 units on a 600V architecture, for 540 kWh of total capacity. The brochure specifies 459 kWh of usable energy “across the full battery life,” so Prevost is holding back about 15% as a buffer.
The six Volvo Cube2 battery units in the H3-45 Electric (Image: Prevost)
The packs are liquid-cooled and IP6K9K-rated, and they use the same VCS2B coolant as the diesel H3-45. Volvo also backs every battery for refurbishment, second life, or recycling.
Prevost rates the coach at “up to 250 miles (400 km)” of range. But the footnote under that number says typical energy use runs up to 2.25 kWh per mile (1.40 kWh/km).
Do the math with Prevost’s own figures: 459 kWh of usable energy at 2.25 kWh/mile is about 204 miles, or roughly 328 km. Reaching 250 miles requires averaging about 1.84 kWh/mile. So 250 miles is the best case, and operators should plan around closer to 200 miles before keeping any reserve for the return to the depot.
Also, an energy buffer of almost 80 kWh is quite massive.
CCS1 and MCS, both standard
On a CCS1 charger at up to 350 kW, a 20-80% charge takes about 55 minutes, according to Prevost. The Megawatt Charging System (MCS) cuts that to about 35 minutes. The charge port is positioned for pull-through truck-stop stalls, and Prevost says no adapter is needed on public networks.
Charging the H3-45 Electric (Image: Prevost)
Those numbers also tell you how fast MCS actually charges this coach. Going from 20% to 80% of 459 kWh means adding about 275 kWh. Doing that in 35 minutes averages roughly 470 kW. That’s a lot faster than CCS1, but nowhere near a megawatt.
The value of MCS here is access as much as speed. Megawatt chargers are being built for electric semi trucks, like the first MCS truck charge in North America at EV Realty’s San Bernardino hub , and newer dispensers like Kempower’s dual CCS and MCS charger serve both connectors. A coach that can pull into those stalls has a lot more charging options on the highway.
Same coach, different powertrain
The rest of the spec sheet reads like a regular H3-45: up to 52 passengers, Cloud One Premium seating, Prevost Driver Assist, LED headlights, five monitors, automatic tag-axle unload, and a kneeling system. 360-degree cameras and a winter package are optional.
Prevost H3-45 Electric (Image: Prevost)
Prevost markets the coach as a certified zero-emission vehicle and leans hard on grant eligibility in its brochure. There’s one catch in the fine print. The optional cold-weather heater is diesel-fired, and it produces emissions when it runs. For Canadian and northern US operators, that’s probably the option most of them will tick.
Prevost didn’t include pricing or a delivery date in its announcement. Jay Menard, who runs Prevost’s ZEV programs, told Electric Autonomy that pilots start in early 2027 and that production deliveries should begin around mid-August 2027.
Five years behind MCI
Prevost isn’t first here. Its main North American rival, MCI, unveiled its J4500 CHARGE electric coach in 2021 with a 544 kWh battery and more than 200 miles of rated range. So Prevost is arriving about five years later with essentially the same battery size.
What Prevost brings is a single-OEM drivetrain from Volvo, more power, a multi-speed gearbox, and MCS. It also keeps the electric version on the same platform as the diesel H3-45. And Prevost confirmed in September that its 2027 Volvo D13 diesel meets the new EPA and CARB standards. The diesel H3-45 isn’t going anywhere.

Meet the BYD Whale, a new flagship electric minivan
The Whale is the first flagship multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) from BYD’s Ocean series. BYD has several sub-brands, including Denza, Yangwang, and Fang Cheng Bao, and sells vehicles under two primary lineups: Ocean and Dynasty.
BYD unveiled the Whale for the first time at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, with a launch set for the first quarter of 2027.
Measuring 5,270 mm long, 1,996 mm wide, and 1,815 mm tall, with a 3,130 mm wheelbase, BYD’s newest minivan is slightly longer than the Chrysler Pacifica.

The Whale will be available in both plug-in hybrid (PHEV) and pure electric (EV) powertrains. Both will use BYD’s latest Blade Batteries 2.0. The PHEV version will offer a pure-electric CLTC range of 248 miles (400 km), while the EV variant offers over 559 miles (900 km) of range on a single charge.

Leading up to its debut, camouflaged prototypes were spotted with a boxy design that looked closer to a traditional gas-powered MPV.

BYD didn’t reveal many details outside of confirming the name and showcasing the design. With LiDAR on the roof, the Whale will offer BYD’s latest Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS).
The Whale will go on sale in the first quarter of 2027, joining the Dynasty Series Xia, Linghui M9, and Denza D9 as BYD’s fourth MPV.

Ford's Valencia Plant in Spain Is Becoming Part of Geely's European Strategy
10 photos
Photo: Geely
Europe's automotive industry has previously ignored Chinese newcomers. Things changed dramatically once those Chinese automakers started taking market share for themselves across the continent that gave us the likes of Volkswagen, Fiat, Citroen, and Volvo.
As far as Geely is concerned, the manufacturer's latest move can be summed up like this: why keep importing vehicles from China when you can use European factories controlled by your European competition?
Michael Yang, the managing director of Geely Auto UK, told Automotive News that a new electric vehicle architecture will be localized at Ford 's plant in Valencia, Spain. Production should kick off in 2028. While Yang did not identify said platform or which models would use it, his announcement speaks volumes.
To bypass steep EU import tariffs on battery-electric vehicles and avoid caps on hybrid imports from China, both Leapmotor and BYD decided on building cars inside Europe. The lesser Chinese automaker took the fastest route, partnering with Stellantis to build the B10 crossover at the Zaragoza plant in Spain.
Because said facility takes care of stamping, welding, and painting with over 40 percent local content, Leapmotor's Stellantis-built vehicles qualify as made in Europe, thus dodging import duties. BYD, on the other hand, chose to build its own plant from the ground up in Szeged, Hungary. As if that wasn't enough, BYD is also planning to acquire Ineos Automotive's Hambach facility in France.
Per available information, Ford will own 66 percent of the proposed joint venture with Geely. This arrangement gives the Chinese manufacturer access to an established vehicle assembly operation while the Dearborn-based partner fills capacity, spreading the cost of running such a major production complex. The Valencia site has the potential to make around 500,000 vehicles per annum.
Photo: Geely Considering that core Geely models for Europe are presently based on the Global Intelligent Electric Architecture and its Evo upgrade, the GEA Evo could very well be the multi-energy platform intended for the Valencia plant. In any case, Geely wants to sell 16 models in the European Union by 2028.
Yang also made it clear that Geely, which owns Volvo, intends to use Volvo's European manufacturing network to hit its 16-model target by 2028. Additions include a city car, smaller crossovers, and larger utility vehicles, including a full-size model. Just like Leapmotor and BYD, local production is the name of the game here. The attraction is terribly simple to understand.
China is already oversaturated, while European automakers continue to ignore European demand for cheap-and-cheerful vehicles. Even after accounting for tariffs and quotas, Chinese automakers manage to undercut European rivals, with price being key to the popularity of Chinese brands in said part of the world.
Building locally would help Geely shorten the supply chain, save money using European industrial capacity, and put Geely closer to European dealer networks. Having a manufacturing operation in Europe can also change how the customer perceives a given vehicle, and that's really bad news for the establishment.
Even though interests overlap, neither side pretends that this is an altruistic situation. Europe and its automakers need factories humming, workers working, and investments to keep things moving in the right direction. Chinese manufacturers need access without absorbing trade restrictions along the way.

What would you do, and how would you feel knowing you have 72 hours to complete a task that just landed in your lap, under the threat of losing your job right before Thanksgiving? (Talk about completely F-ing up the timing. F is for Friday, by the way. Which is today, because that's when the deadline expires).
That high-stakes ultimatum hit Adam, WD Detailing’s trusty mechanic, who got the scare straight from RJ while contemplating a Rounded Line square-body. The 1987 Chevrolet R20 Silverado regular-cab long-bed was dragged out of a remote barn after 15 years of neglect. Somehow, pickup truck years put against car years seem to be the equivalent of dog years compared to human years. for every years that passes over a passenger car, it looks like seven have trampled over the humble utilitarian.
Flat tires carved deep trenches across the dirt floor during extraction. The crew's mission was brutal: detail the heavy-duty hauler spotless and make it start, idle, drive, and stop within 72 hours.
Before diving under the hood, pause and wonder how a bare-bones wooden cargo box bolted behind an exposed cab became America's defining machine. Born from early twentieth-century farm necessity, the pickup truck quickly escaped barnyards and conquered highways, construction sites, and suburban driveways alike.
Photo: YouTube/WD Detailing Detroit realized that utility could carry swagger, turning honest steel haulers into cultural icons that outlived chrome-drenched coupes and anchored the Motor City's bottom line for more than a century. Chevrolet joined that march in 1918 with its One-Ton Truck, followed by prewar breakthroughs like the 1929 Stovebolt inline-six and the stylish 1938 half-ton.
Postwar evolution brought the Advance Design line from 1947 to 1955 and Task Force pickups through 1959. Next came four C/K generations—1960–1966, Action Line 1967–1972, square-body Rounded Line 1973–1987, and GMT400 1988–2000—before five Silverado generations spanning GMT800, GMT900, K2XX, T1XX, and the redesigned 2027 truck.
That brings us to 1987, a pivotal swan song when General Motors renamed two-wheel-drive C-series trucks to R and four-wheel-drive K-series models to V because the incoming 1988 GMT400 debuted early in April 1987. Shortened regular-cab production totaled 269,763 Chevrolet R/V pickups: 183,857 half-ton R10 and V10 trucks, 53,522 three-quarter-ton R20 and V20 haulers, and 32,384 one-ton R30 and V30 workhorses.
Hardly exotic when new, three-quarter-ton survivors remain far scarcer than half-tons today.
Photo: YouTube/WD Detailing For 1987, Chevrolet also introduced throttle-body electronic fuel injection across its entire gasoline pickup lineup. Buyers chose between a 4.3-liter Vortec V6 with 160 hp, a 5.0-liter V8 delivering 170 hp, a 5.7-liter V8 rated at 210 hp under 8,600 pounds GVWR or 185 hp in heavy-duty trim, and a 7.4-liter big-block packing 230 hp. Diesel loyalists got a 6.2-liter V8 producing 130 hp or 148 hp in heavy-duty specification.
Transmission options spanned a 3-speed Saginaw manual, a 4-speed New Process NP833 overdrive manual, the heavy-duty 4-speed Muncie SM465 manual with a granny-low gear—the exact stick bolted inside this rescued truck—plus 3-speed Turbo Hydra-Matic 400 and 4-speed 700R4 overdrive automatics. Back in 1987, a standard two-wheel-drive R20 Fleetside long-bed started at $10,530, rising to $11,211 in upscale Silverado trim like this example, or $12,629 for the heavy-duty R20 HD Silverado.
Once the 72-hour countdown started, Adam popped the hood to grim news: no radiator, pitch-black oil, and throttle-body injection instead of a simple carburetor. The 350-cubic-inch V8 cranked with spark and barked briefly on hand-poured fuel, yet the fuel pump stayed silent. Underneath lurked a detached exhaust pipe, a rogue soup can, a missing driver-side tank, a dry rear brake reservoir, and a rusted-solid rear brake drum Adam finally hammered free before hunting parts.
Photo: YouTube/WD Detailing With 60 hours remaining, RJ Wagner attacked 15 years of barn leaves packed in the bed and revived the rust-stained white eight-lug steelies with hydrofluoric acid and iron remover. Then came a painful plot twist: a polish test turned his yellow microfiber red, confirming fragile single-stage enamel without clear coat. Chemical pre-wash was off the table, forcing slow rinsing, engine-bay degreasing, contact washes, and clay-mitting that burned the clock down to 48 hours.
Morning arrived with 36 hours left and a biohazard cabin waiting inside. RJ unbolted the rodent-trailed bucket seats, Tornador-blasted clouds of dust from the maroon carpet, evicted a mouse nest packed inside the glove box, and scrubbed sticky decades of grime off the steering wheel. Just as exhaustion peaked at 30 hours remaining, WD Garage's Mike burst in to drill-brush and extract the carpets, fragile cloth seats, and rubber GM floor mats past nightfall.
On the final morning, only 12 hours stood between triumph and an embarrassing Black Friday flop. RJ cut through chalky orange oxidation with a wool pad, resurrecting razor-sharp cherry-red reflections across the Squarebody panels. With seven hours left, Adam strolled back holding a radiator, fuel pump, injectors, and battery. Dropping the surviving passenger tank exposed a disintegrated non-fuel-rated hose and stale red gasoline, yet they bolted the rebuilt tank right back up without testing it.
Photo: YouTube/WD Detailing Sure enough, after sealing the paint and installing the radiator, turning the key with 2.5 hours left brought dead silence. Rather than dropping the tank again, Adam applied direct power, proved the pump ran, traced a broken firewall harness plug, and bypassed it to wake the pump. Still, zero fuel sprayed with one hour and 25 minutes left, until a noid light confirmed computer pulse and two fresh injectors fired the 350 to life.
With the brakes finally bled and the video due at the editor's desk ahead of its 12-hour release window, RJ slid behind the clean wheel and rolled the cherry-red 1987 Silverado 20 into the cold night. Shifting smoothly down the street and stopping on command sealed the miracle. Adam saved his paycheck, the WD Detailing crew brought home their figurative bacon, and another forgotten three-quarter-ton Squarebody proved Detroit iron never goes quietly.

A Motorhome to Ride Out the Apocalypse: This 1980 MAN KAT1 Conversion Wants Your Attention
45 photos
Photo: Car And Classic
No one likes preparing for the worst, there are no finer ways for doing that than with this motorhome, which seems perfect to ride out the apocalypse in. Though it wasn't intentionally designed to withstand whatever the end of times might bring, this 1980 MAN KAT1 motorhome conversion is bound to do just that.
In these troubled times, making a sensible decision is a must. This motorhome won't be that from a financial perspective, but if you're an all doom and gloom type, it would probably feel that way in terms of preparing for the worst.
This overland motorhome isn't just badass enough to handle the collapse of civilization, however it might happen, but it's also a certified historic vehicle, though that last part will mean nothing when the zombies come.
But let's not start this on a negative note. This is a 1980 MAN KAT1 motorhome conversion, with the base vehicle registered as a historic vehicle and coming with the proper documentation and the conversion being a more recent, bespoke job.
Photo: Car And Classic The rig is up for sale on auction through the Car and Classic platform and is now located in Aquitaine, France, where it spent the last four years inside a garage . The current owner bought it in 2022 and oversaw its conversion into a motorhome, and he says that the rig as it is has never been used for overlanding. Photos in the gallery show that it's been appointed for that purpose, even if it never got to fulfill it.
The base of the rig is MAN KAT1, described as "the most renowned military truck platforms for its offroad ability." Even that's an understatement: in production between 1977 and 1983 and offered in 4x4, 6x6, and 8x8 variants, it's the most badass military vehicle produced.
Development for it started as early as 1962, when the West German military announced the intention to replace the aging fleet. Because the list of requirements was so vast and ultimately impossible to check in its entirety, the military asked manufacturers to pool their resources, leading to the foundation of a joint development bureau under MAN.
Photo: Car And Classic During the production years, 10,424 MAN KAT1 units would be built, 3,601 of which would be 4x4s. This was one of them, and the seller is offering full documentation for its military past, including its logbook with personnel transport missions.
For the motorhome conversion, the seller prepped the base vehicle with a full restoration, which included sandblasting and repainting the chassis. The bespoke "living cell" is a four-person home that's fully self-contained – which is to be expected whenever you speak of an overlander but still feels one notch above the rest.
Access inside is done via a solid metal staircase, through a magnet flyscreen, directly into the main living space. Though you can tell from a first glance, it offers sleeping for four people, though it seems only one of the bunks is already prepped for that. The other appears empty and could double as extra storage room.
Photo: Car And Classic So, you get dual enclosed bunks in front of the entryway, a bathroom at the front, a full kitchen on the campside, and a booth dinette that will drop into a bed across the way.
Features are exactly what you'd expect for a "self-contained" RV: a roof lined fully with solar panels, a Victron Energy control unit, a massive battery pack, holding tanks, a Truma Sapphire Compact AC, heater, and the full range of appliances. Unfortunately, the seller doesn't offer exact figures for the solar, battery, or holding tanks.
Everything runs off solar, including kitchen appliances. The large counter integrates a two-burner induction cooktop, a small oven, a compact dishwasher, a mini washing machine (probably a 3 or 4-kg/6.6 or 8.8-lb one), and a 12V fridge. You also get plenty of workspace in here for meal prep and sufficient storage both for kitchen utensils and dry goods.
Photo: Car And Classic The bathroom is a full one as well, with a plumbed toilet, a sink on a vanity, a heated towel rack right above the toilet, and a nice glass-encased shower. It's the most luxurious part of the build, but that doesn't mean that the rest of the space is ugly or cheap in any way. It's rather in keeping with the beefed up exterior, with an emphasis on functionality and space, not necessarily aesthetics.
Also included with the build is a large screen TV, dedicated storage inside the bunks, water filtration, a premium Froli-like system on top of the slatted base of the upper bunk, and plenty of lockable metal lockers outside.
Power for this motorhome comes from the original naturally aspirated 12.8-liter air-cooled Deutz V8 diesel engine located behind the cab and delivering 252 hp and 579 lb ft (785 Nm) of torque. The rig has a 6-speed ZF transmission, permanent four-wheel drive, locking differentials, and hub-reduction gears.
Photo: Car And Classic The seller notes that the paintjob shows some imperfections, as does the three-person cab, particularly on the double seat. The odometer reads 18,484 km (11,485 miles), but as already mentioned, the current owner added nothing to it since they kept the motorhome inside a garage.
The current bid is €8,000 (approximately $8,750 at the current exchange rate) with 6 more days to go into the auction , but reserve hasn't even been met.

By: Staff Writer November 27, 2026
Saudi Arabia is preparing to postpone its Future Minerals Forum as regional attacks threaten the January gathering, The Financial Times reported Thursday.
Organizers have warned speakers and participants that the Riyadh event will likely need to be rescheduled, according to the newspaper.
The forum told the newspaper it had not been cancelled and that updates would come through official channels.
As of Friday, the event’s website was continuing to advertise the Jan. 12–14 dates.
The uncertainty follows a Houthi attack on the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in Riyadh on Tuesday that injured 11 people, the FT reported.
Other major Saudi events have already shifted. Cityscape Global’s organizers moved the real estate exhibition from November to Feb. 1–4, 2027. The Global Health Exhibition has also been deferred until October 2027.
Mining ambitions
Saudi Arabia has hosted five editions of the forum, which brings together governments, mining companies and investors to discuss mineral supply and development.
The January 2026 gathering drew 21,500 participants and produced 132 agreements and memorandums of understanding valued at 100 billion Saudi riyals, or about $26.7 billion (C$37.9 billion), organizers said. Its ministerial roundtable included representatives from 91 countries.
Past speakers included executives from BHP (ASX, LSE: BHP), Rio Tinto (ASX, LSE: RIO), Vale (NYSE: VALE) and Chilean state-owned miner Codelco.
The published 2027 program carries the theme “global collaboration for resilient mineral supply,” with a ministerial roundtable and discussions on investment, innovation and minerals policy.
Under Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia is seeking to reduce its reliance on oil by expanding other industries. Mining is intended to become a third pillar of industrial development alongside oil and petrochemicals.
The forum is part of that effort to attract investment and build mining partnerships across Africa, Western Asia and Central Asia. Print

There is a stark difference between the histories of the two companies named 2026 Best Places to Work in the Power Industry. Babcock & Wilcox (B&W) was founded in 1867 by two friends who designed the first inherently safe water-tube boiler. BrilliT is an information technology (IT) firm formed in 2022 inside an electric cooperative. B&W has about 1,650 employees worldwide, although it entered through its Akron, Ohio, headquarters, which had 471 employees at the time of the survey. BrilliT, which also won in 2025, has 31. Both are recognized for reasons that overlap more than their background and size might suggest.
Now in its third year, the program, conducted with Best Companies Group (BCG), recognizes employers based on employee surveys and a detailed look at workplace policies. The submissions B&W and BrilliT provided to BCG describe workplaces where pay, time off, and a clear path for advancement form the foundation. B&W builds on that foundation with flexible scheduling, regular access to senior leaders, and a long list of programs designed to make the workday more enjoyable.
To be eligible, power companies and the vendors that serve them must have at least 15 full- or part-time employees in the U.S. or Canada and have been in business for at least a year. Organizations may enter as a single location, in which case the location appears in their name on the list. B&W entered as “The Babcock & Wilcox Company (Akron, Ohio Headquarters).” B&W said the programs described below are offered across the U.S. and Canada and at many of its international locations.
Participants complete two parts, and both are required. Employers answer a questionnaire about policies, practices, and demographics. Employees take an online engagement and satisfaction survey of roughly 77 statements, plus several open-ended and demographic questions. BCG then analyzes the data and ranks the participating organizations. The descriptions quoted below come from the winners’ submissions to BCG.
Pay, Advancement, and Time Off
BrilliT, a wholly owned subsidiary of Rappahannock Electric Cooperative (REC), manages the IT infrastructure, networking, and security for all of the cooperative’s technology assets. REC is a member-owned utility serving more than 185,000 connections in portions of 22 counties in Virginia. BrilliT said its employees would point first to pay and benefits and to opportunities for promotion. Among its less common offerings, the company listed tuition reimbursement and a generous vacation and sick leave policy.
BrilliT’s winner profile stresses its familiarity with its utility customer. “We know first-hand what keeps electric utility leaders and employees up at night,” the company said, adding that “our clients need a partner as invested as they are in their company, community, and future.” Its leadership has decades of combined experience in both the energy and IT industries. “Our networks are full of smart, dedicated people,” BrilliT said.
B&W’s list is similar on the fundamentals. The company cited competitive compensation, bonuses, a 401(k), flexible health plan options, and career development “with a focus on promoting from within.” It also pointed to incentive and recognition programs “to help reinforce to employees they are valued and valuable contributors to our company.” On time off, B&W said it offers generous vacation, including a paid end-of-year shutdown from Christmas through New Year’s Day, though some areas follow alternate schedules to maintain service.
Flexibility, Culture, and Perks
Where B&W goes further is in how, and where, employees do their work. Its Responsible and Flexible Workplace Program, known as ReFlex, gives employees flexibility in their work hours. Employees also choose their work location, with the option of working 100% remotely, in the office, or in a hybrid arrangement. B&W put both of those programs among the top three things its employees would say they love.
The company also invests heavily in making sure employees know where the business is headed. B&W’s communication programs include an intranet updated daily, quarterly all-employee addresses by senior leadership, and an Executive Lunch Program in which senior leaders meet monthly with a group of employees in a casual setting. A separate question and answer program lets employees submit questions electronically and receive answers from the appropriate decision maker.
B&W’s other programs are meant to build camaraderie. Free lunches, donut and ice cream socials, and raffles for tickets to sporting events are common. The workplace includes a ping-pong table and golf simulator, with an arcade game on the way, and team wins are celebrated with free popcorn, donuts, or other snacks.
Its Children’s Holiday Program is more unusual. Employees’ children through age 11 receive a customized letter from Santa that includes input from their parent about the child’s interests, accomplishments, and gift wishes, along with a $25 gift card. B&W also coordinates volunteer activities on company time, including Earth Day cleanups, Food Bank volunteering, Adopt-a-Family, and the United Way “Day of Caring.”
For all of its programs, B&W’s most telling claim is about longevity. “Our employees consistently tell us that B&W is a place where they can build an entire career,” the company said, noting that it has “quite a few ‘generational employees’ whose grandparents and parents have also worked for our company.” B&W said its success is rooted in teamwork, “a value dating to its earliest days.”
Plenty of employers now offer flexible schedules and free lunches. Fewer can say that a family keeps coming back to the same employer, and that may be the strongest evidence of a good workplace in either company’s submission.
—Aaron Larson is POWER’s executive editor.

EIB and IDC officials sign the financing agreement on Thursday, Nov. 26. Credit: European Investment Bank.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 27, 2026
The European Investment Bank (EIB) and South Africa’s Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) agreed to jointly provide up to €300 million (US$327 million) to advance African critical minerals projects, linking investment in local processing and industry with Europe’s efforts to diversify supplies.
Announced Thursday, the facility is expected to support around €900 million in total investment, according to the EIB. It’s consistent with South Africa’s 2025 Critical Minerals Strategy , which aims to process more minerals locally and expand the country’s role in supplying global industries.
“Ultimately, this facility is about turning our mineral wealth into factories, skills and jobs,” IDC CEO Mmakgoshi Lekhethe said in a statement .
By enabling investment in strategic minerals and related industries, the financing “will contribute to economic growth, value creation and greater supply chain resilience for both Africa and Europe,” added EIB Vice-President Ambroise Fayolle, who signed the agreement on behalf of the Luxembourg-based lender.
Eligible activities range from extraction and processing to refining, recycling and substitution, along with supporting energy, transport and digital infrastructure. Projects in South Africa and other sub-Saharan African countries must contribute to local industrial development and demonstrate a clear connection to European value chains, the EIB said.
Access to capital
For developers, infrastructure funding could help address financing needs that extend beyond the boundaries of a mine or a processing plant.
The deal addresses a major obstacle to developing the continent’s mineral resources: access to long-term capital at competitive prices. Its emphasis on beneficiation and downstream processing aims to build local industrial capacity and employment while attracting other investors into projects, according to the IDC.
The facility is the EIB’s first dedicated critical minerals financing operation outside the European Union under the strategic initiative it launched in 2025. The announcement didn’t identify project recipients or disclose individual loan allocations. Projects are expected to meet international environmental and social standards.
Close to home
South Africa’s critical minerals and metals strategy calls for more exploration, processing close to mines, power and infrastructure investments as well as financial instruments, according to the mineral resources department.
The strategy also prioritizes research, skills and regional integration. Its industrial objective is to increase the value retained from mineral production through stronger domestic manufacturing and a broader export base, rather than relying principally on overseas processing, the department’s announcement explained.
The new financing follows a November 2025 accord between the European Union and South Africa on sustainable minerals and metals value chains. That partnership was signed alongside a clean trade and investment agreement, placing minerals within a wider effort to strengthen industrial links and investment between the two economies, according to the European Council.
Africa focus
The EIB has already backed preparatory work elsewhere in Africa. In February, it announced agreements offering Andrada Mining and EcoGraf up to €2 million each in technical assistance.
The support covers Andrada’s expansion into lithium in Namibia and EcoGraf’s natural graphite development in Tanzania, including engineering, infrastructure and environmental work to improve investment readiness.
Friday’s announcement extends a busy week for the bank’s minerals financing. On Wednesday, the EIB agreed to invest about €400 million in Polish miner KGHM to support deeper copper deposits, underground transport and processing upgrades, reinforcing its parallel push to secure production within Europe.

Braim Chiple. ( Image courtesy of International Copper Association. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 27, 2026
Codelco Chief Commercial Officer Braim Chiple has resigned to join commodity trader Trafigura Group, Bloomberg reported Friday, as the Chilean state-owned copper miner reshapes its leadership under CEO Jorge Gómez.
Carlos Olavarría, currently Codelco’s refined copper commercial manager, will succeed Chiple on Jan. 1, 2027, the miner said Thursday . Chiple has headed its commercial operations since 2024.
The departing executive will take a Chile-based role at Trafigura, Bloomberg reported, citing three people familiar with the matter. Trafigura declined to comment to the news agency. The trader disclosed full ownership of Chile’s Minera Altair in its half-year report.
Olavarría will take over as Codelco seeks to diversify refined copper sales after inventories swelled in the United States ahead of possible tariffs, Bloomberg reported.
Codelco also named James Galatoire vice-president of projects, effective Dec. 1. He has led Collahuasi’s expansion project since 2024, adding another executive from the operation Gómez previously ran.
Paulina Andreoli, currently risk and sustainability manager at iron ore producer Compañía Minera del Pacífico, will become general manager of Codelco’s Ventanas division on Dec. 14.
Financial discipline
Under Chairman Bernardo Fontaine , Codelco is emphasizing profitable production and stronger controls as it investigates irregularities in its production records.
The company preliminarily identified 42,100 tonnes of copper improperly recorded as production in 2024 and 2025, with a potential accounting impact of $120 million (C$170 million) to $140 million. KPMG and EY audits remain under way, according to disclosures this month.
Codelco had invested $32 billion over eight years while output declined, Fontaine said. He put the company’s costs at 78% above those of multinational peers, Emol reported Nov. 9, citing his interview with Chilean radio station Duna .
The chairman argues that private partnerships are needed to sustain production and develop unworked mineral holdings. He reiterated that approach at Asia Copper Week this month, calling for more exploration and collaboration.
Existing partnerships include the Anillo exploration project with BHP (ASX, LSE: BHP), Nuevo Cobre with Rio Tinto (ASX, LSE: RIO), and a joint mine plan for Codelco’s Andina and Anglo American’s (LSE: AAL) neighbouring Los Bronces operation. Print

The Toyota Highlander 9X will go on sale in early 2027 as the brand’s first extended-range electric vehicle with advanced new tech from Huawei and CATL.
Toyota’s first EREV arrives as the Highlander 9X in 2027
Toyota joins Hyundai Motor Group, including Kia and Genesis, Ford, Volkswagen, and several other major OEMs with plans to launch its first EREV in the first quarter of 2027.
Toyota’s Chinese joint venture, GAC Toyota, announced at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27 that the EREV will use its flagship SUV nameplate, the Highlander 9X, when it arrives.
The Highlander 9X will blend Toyota’s classic global car heritage with some of China’s most advanced technology.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
At the event, GAC Toyota revealed that the flagship EREV will use a battery custom-developed through its partnership with CATL, along with Huawei’s advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) and smart cockpit setup.
The EREV will be Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, joining battery electric vehicles (BEVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).
GAC Toyota previews first extended-range EV, the Highlander 9X (Source: GAC Toyota)
Unlike fully electric vehicles, EREVs have a small gas engine that acts as a generator to charge the battery when it gets low, extending driving range.
According to Nikkei , Toyota aims to produce 200,000 EREVs in China in 2027, and about 400,000 units in 2028.
We will have to wait until closer to launch for battery and powertrain specifics, but local reports suggest Toyota’s EREV will deliver a combined CTLC range of over 621 miles (1,000 km) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.
You can catch a glimpse of what appears to be the extended-range vehicle in the video GAC Toyota posted confirming the new EREV tech.
Since the Highlander 9X will be built in China, Toyota will not sell the EREV in the US. Instead, it will launch the fully electric Highlander BEV in the US in 2027.
The all-electric Toyota Highlander BEV will be available with front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive powertrains with two battery packs: 77 kWh or 95.8 kWh. The smaller (77 kWh) battery provides up to 287 miles of EPA-estimated range, while the larger (95.8 kWh) battery provides up to 320 miles in FWD models.
Like the outgoing version, the fifth-generation electric Toyota Highlander will offer three rows of seating and space for seven passengers.
